D017_l001.question:
A 34-year-old married male firefighter presents with a chronic preoccupation with perceived defects in his facial appearance, ongoing for several years. He reports excessive concern regarding the shape and proportion of his nose and eyes, describing them as abnormal or disfiguring, despite reassurances from others and normal appearance on clinical observation.

Over this period, he has pursued multiple cosmetic consultations and has undergone several facial procedures and dermatologic interventions aimed at correcting these perceived flaws, with only transient or no relief in distress. He spends significant time checking mirrors, comparing his face to others, and mentally reviewing perceived imperfections.

These concerns cause marked distress and have led to functional impairment, including avoidance of social interactions outside of work, reluctance to participate in team-related social activities, and difficulty concentrating when off duty due to persistent ruminations about his appearance. He denies psychotic symptoms, substance use contributing to symptoms, or a history of neurological illness. There is no evidence of a major medical condition explaining his appearance concerns.
D017_l001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D017_l002.question:

She reports a persistent belief that her body is inadequately developed and insufficiently muscular despite reassurance from others and objective findings within normal limits. She spends significant time scrutinizing her physique, including frequent mirror checking and comparative evaluation of her body to others.

The patient describes ongoing dissatisfaction with specific perceived physical flaws and has repeatedly pursued cosmetic and dermatologic interventions in an effort to correct these concerns, with only transient relief and rapid recurrence of distress about her appearance.
